item.title: Ep 1 – A thousand fewer paths (6 Nov 2026)
item.description:
A thousand fewer paths: OpenAI's autonomous pipeline validates 948 Linux local-privilege-escalation bugs for about $1.2M in API credits and ships GPT-6 Cyber to Daybreak Red defenders; Cognition releases SWE-2 Flash inside Devin at one-fifth SWE-2's price but keeps weights gated; Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview takes a US open-weight lead on agentic coding under Apache 2.0.

  • A thousand fewer paths to root (OpenAI, 4 Nov): scout agents narrowed Linux to ~7% of the codebase (~2.8M LOC); analysts produced 2,308 candidates in 12 hours; validation reproduced 1,724 (~74.7%); exploit agents on stock desktop VMs with KASLR/SMEP/SMAP produced 1,169 working LPE exploits → 948 distinct vulnerabilities with candidate patches; run cost $1,213,430 (~$1,279 per LPE); vs historical Pwn2Own ($20k) / TyphoonPWN ($70k) LPE bounties ≈16–55× cheaper; ≥10 novel exploitation techniques in a sampled set; July GPT-5.6 Sol run found 166 LPEs. HN discussion.
  • GPT-6 Cyber (OpenAI, 5 Nov): ExploitGym 48.5% (was 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, ~51% relative gain); Preparedness Framework cybersecurity Critical (up from High); out-of-scope honeypot avoidance 99.93% without deployment prompts / 100% with; 81 novel high-severity Firefox vulns (Mozilla shipping fixes); RemoteExploitBench 95% for Cyber vs 100% refuse for Astra+Daybreak Blue; initially for approved Daybreak Red API/Codex customers. Coverage: SecurityWeek, Phoronix, Axios.
  • Introducing SWE-2 Flash (Cognition, 4 Nov): post-train of Thinking Machines Inkling-Small (276B-A12B); mid-training before RL → Terminal-Bench 4.0 0.9%→20.0%, FrontierCode 2.0 3.2%→24.0%; claims 1/5 price and 3× speed of SWE-2 (replayed ~200 vs 60 tok/s); free in Devin Desktop/CLI for Pro/Max/Teams through 30 Nov; ExploitBench 11.3%→34.8%; weights not public — partner sharing programme planned. Context: OrcaRouter, AI Affairs.
  • Ripple-65B Preview (Ricursive Intelligence): dense 65B Transformer, 12T pretraining tokens, up to 1M context, Apache 2.0; Terminal-Bench 2.1 80.52 (US open-weight SOTA vs Reflection Beam 501B 80.1, Muse Spark Open 816B 76.4, Inkling 975B 63.8, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B 56.4); full R&D ~$32M (~1/10 prior open-weight coding SOTA estimate); 1.4M RL rollouts (~70× fewer than Beam); on Hugging Face, Together, Fireworks, OpenRouter, GMI Cloud. VentureBeat, Hugging Face.

Narrated by William and Natasha.

Music: “Evening Glow”, “What's Behind the Door”, “Curiousity”, “Tech Toys”, “Under Suspicion”, “Bigger Questions”, “Something To Fill The Space”, “More On That Later” by Lee Rosevere (CC BY 4.0), via Free Music Archive; trimmed, looped and edited for this show. Sound effects: “Air whoosh” by pyranostudios (CC0 1.0).

Transcript

B: Nine hundred and forty-eight.

B: That is how many distinct ways an OpenAI pipeline turned a low-privilege Linux login into root. The API bill: one point two million dollars.

* * *

B: Hello and welcome to Almost Human 365. I'm Natasha.

A: And I'm William. It's Friday the sixth of November.

B: Today: nearly a thousand paths to root, Cognition's cheaper coding model that still won't open its weights, and a sixty-five-billion open model claiming the US coding lead.

* * *

A: OpenAI's write-up is titled "A thousand fewer paths to root." Scout agents cut the Linux kernel to about seven percent of its code, the parts a low-privileged user can reach. Analysts produced two thousand three hundred and eight candidates in twelve hours. Validation reproduced one thousand seven hundred and twenty-four, about three-quarters.

B: On stock desktop VMs with KASLR, SMEP and SMAP on, exploit agents built one thousand one hundred and sixty-nine working local root exploits. After variant analysis: nine hundred and forty-eight distinct bugs, with candidate patches.

A: Cost: one point two million in API credits, about twelve hundred and seventy-nine dollars each. Against historical Pwn2Own bounties, roughly sixteen to fifty-five times cheaper than buying the same finds.

B: Same week, GPT-6 Cyber: forty-eight point five percent on ExploitGym, up from thirty-two point one. Preparedness: Critical for cyber, up from High. Daybreak Red customers first.

A: Why this news is important: proving kernel bugs is now a pipeline cost. Patching has to keep the same pace.

* * *

B: Cognition shipped SWE-2 Flash in Devin Desktop and the CLI. Base: Thinking Machines' Inkling-Small, two hundred and seventy-six billion total, twelve billion active. Mid-training before RL lifted Terminal-Bench 4.0 from zero point nine percent to twenty, and FrontierCode 2.0 from three point two to twenty-four.

A: Pitch: one-fifth the price and three times the speed of SWE-2, free for Pro, Max and Teams through the thirtieth of November.

B: Weights stay closed. Cyber training raised ExploitBench from eleven point three to thirty-four point eight percent, so Cognition is building a partner sharing programme instead of a public dump.

A: Why this news is important: everyday agent work is moving to smaller models, and "American open weights" increasingly means gated partners, not a Hugging Face download.

* * *

A: Same week, the opposite move. Ricursive released Ripple-65B Preview under Apache 2.0: dense, sixty-five billion parameters, twelve trillion pretraining tokens, up to a million of context. It reports eighty point five on Terminal-Bench 2.1, ahead of Reflection Beam at five hundred and one billion and Meta's Muse Spark Open at eight hundred and sixteen billion.

B: Full R and D from scratch: thirty-two million dollars, about a tenth of Ricursive's estimate for the prior open-weight coding SOTA.

A: On Hugging Face and via Together, Fireworks and OpenRouter.

B: Why this news is important: US open-weight coding is no longer only giant MoEs. A smaller dense model with open weights now competes on agentic terminal work.

* * *

B: Nine hundred and forty-eight paths closed this week. Sources are in the notes. Have a great weekend. See you Monday.
